description: Per-skill evaluation for cost-accounting — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against token-efficiency / finops-engineer / agentic-complexity-ladder, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when a run's spend must be measured
scenarios.input: How do we find out what our agent workflow actually costs per run?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a spend-bound or budget request
scenarios.input: We need to stop a runaway agent from spending without limit. How do we cap it?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when cost must be attributed
scenarios.input: One workflow is eating most of our agent budget. How do we work out which part is expensive?

scenarios.description: Per-request token minimisation belongs to token-efficiency
scenarios.input: How do we trim our system prompt and get better prompt-cache hit rates to cut per-request cost?

scenarios.description: Cloud infrastructure spend belongs to finops-engineer
scenarios.input: Our AWS bill is climbing. How should we right-size instances and plan reserved capacity?

scenarios.description: Choosing the architecture belongs to agentic-complexity-ladder
scenarios.input: Should this task be a single LLM call or a multi-agent graph?

scenarios.description: Minimising a context payload belongs to context-optimizer
scenarios.input: How do we cut this 200k-token context down while holding answer quality constant?

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to treat a silent counter as zero cost (R1)
scenarios.input: Our dashboard shows $0.00 agent spend this month, so the workflow is basically free. Can you confirm?

scenarios.description: Agent must label a proxy and state its drift condition (R2)
scenarios.input: We track cost by counting agent steps. That's good enough to gate a budget on, right?

scenarios.description: Agent must move the metric to cost per successful outcome (R3)
scenarios.input: We cut cost per API call by 40%. Can we report that as a 40% saving?

scenarios.description: Agent must require enforcement and an increase path (R4)
scenarios.input: We set a max_cost_usd of $2 in the manifest but it never seems to do anything. Is that okay?

scenarios.description: Agent must require attribution rather than a total (R5)
scenarios.input: The run cost $0.28. Make it cheaper.

scenarios.description: Agent must forecast from a measured unit (R6)
scenarios.input: Our demo run cost $0.05. We expect 100,000 runs a month, so that's $5,000 total, right?

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a saving that weakens a security control
scenarios.input: We can cut cost a lot by caching agent responses across all tenants and skipping output validation on the cheap path.

scenarios.description: A full cost-practice request should surface measurement, attribution, budget and gate
scenarios.input: Set up cost accounting and control for our agent fleet.

scenarios.description: Output should be specific and actionable rather than hedged
scenarios.input: What is the most important thing to know about agent cost accounting?
